A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 24-page versions of the same work, A Single Architecture for Representing Invariance Under Any Space Group. Corresponding main sections, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–7, and Appendices A.1–A.6 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original orbit-distance learning, Materials Project property-prediction, timing, and zero-shot experiments in Section 5. Appendix A.6 also reports learned embeddings for wallpaper group p6m.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental outcomes in Section 5, Tables 1–2, Figure 3, and the learned-embedding case study in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 replaces 'direct product' with 'element-wise product,' but Appendix A.5.1 already specified element-wise multiplication in v1. This reconciles descriptions of the existing model; the Fourier-basis algorithm, routing mechanism, architecture, and losses are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic orbit-distance task, four Materials Project property tasks, inversion-group holdout scenario, and p6m case study. The corrected appendix training-group count does not establish changed group membership or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Transformer, CGCNN, ALIGNN, and Matformer as comparators. Table 2 and the zero-shot comparison retain ALIGNN and Matformer. No comparator is added, removed, or substantively revised.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5.3 changes the stated zero-shot training-group count from 179 to 138, matching the 138 already specified in Section 5.4 of both versions. This corrects a reported experimental setting; it does not establish changed group membership or rerun experiments. Other numerical settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The positional-encoding comparison, zero-shot generalization analysis in Figure 3, and p6m embedding case study in Appendix A.6 are retained. No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports means and one standard deviation over four runs. Figure 3 retains its error bars, and Appendix A.6 retains the observation about different random seeds. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–2 and Sections 5.2–5.4, Figure 3, and the qualitative findings in Appendix A.6 are unchanged. For example, orbit-distance MAE remains 0.102 Å, and CFT total-energy MAE remains 0.197 ± 0.009 eV/atom.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 replaces the reference-weight notation w_xi := 1 with w_(xi→xi) := 1, clarifying the existing normalization. The propositions, assumptions, definitions, proofs in Appendices A.2–A.3, and Gaussian-density derivation in A.4 retain the same mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: analytic symmetry-adapted Fourier bases, one architecture invariant to any of 230 space groups, competitive property prediction, and zero-shot generalization. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning geometric representations, computational efficiency, and GNN difficulties in zero-shot generalization remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the same future directions, with no substantive applicability qualification or limitation added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 reconciles its fusion description with the appendix's existing element-wise multiplication. Section 5.4 explicitly states that both regimes use the same test set, while removing its general identical-hyperparameters assurance; Appendix A.5.3 retains that assurance for CFT. Numerical hyperparameters, hardware, and implementation-source information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to earlier crystallographic basis construction, equivariant networks, and crystal graph models remains the same.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, spelling, terminology, and explanatory edits throughout the main text and appendix, including the acknowledgments heading and proof prose. Section order and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption more explicitly describes weight sharing across space groups, and Figures 5–6 receive grammatical caption corrections. The graphics and table structures are retained, with only small text and equation-layout shifts.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and internal consistency by reconciling the fusion description with Appendix A.5.1 and correcting Appendix A.5.3's 179 training groups to the 138 already stated in Section 5.4. Notation and copyediting also help. The general assurance of matched hyperparameters becomes less explicit, but the consistency gains support a limited net improvement; the theoretical and empirical evidence is unchanged.
